title: Puka Nacua’s Game‑Time Decision: Calf Injury Leads to Friday DNP, NBC Sports Reports
body:
The Los Angeles Rams placed rookie wide receiver Puka Nacua on the sidelines for Friday’s matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, citing a lingering calf strain that has kept the 22‑year‑old questionable all week. The decision, announced late Thursday, means the Rams will go without one of their most promising offensive weapons as they head into a pivotal Week 7 contest that could determine their playoff trajectory.

Nacua, who burst onto the scene as a fourth‑round pick in 2024 and quickly became a favorite target for quarterback Matthew Stafford, suffered a grade‑one calf strain during the team’s practice on Tuesday. The injury, while not severe enough to warrant surgery, has limited his ability to run routes at full speed and execute the rapid cuts that define his game. Team medical staff evaluated the situation throughout the day and ultimately concluded that the risk of aggravating the strain outweighed the benefit of a rushed return.

The Rams’ offense has leaned heavily on Nacua’s speed and route‑running precision since he joined the roster. In his first six appearances, the rookie logged 28 receptions for 382 yards and three touchdowns, establishing himself as a reliable deep threat and a versatile slot option. His chemistry with Stafford, built on a shared background at the University of Washington, has added a fresh dimension to an offense that struggled to find consistency early in the season. Without Nacua, the Rams will need to lean on veteran receivers Cooper Kupp and Van Jefferson, both of whom have seen a dip in production this year, as well as emerging talent Marquise Brown, who has shown flashes of big‑play ability.

Analysts note that the Raiders, who have been improving defensively under coordinator Patrick Graham, will likely exploit the Rams’ reduced receiving depth. Las Vegas has been effective at pressuring the quarterback and limiting secondary matchups, forcing opponents to rely on tight ends and running backs in the passing game. The Rams’ offensive line, while solid, has shown vulnerability against blitzes, making a quick‑release passing attack—something Nacua thrives in—particularly valuable. Coach Sean McVay’s play‑calling may shift toward a more run‑heavy approach, utilizing running back Kyren Williams and a greater emphasis on play‑action to compensate for the missing weapon.

The decision also reflects a broader trend in the NFL toward cautious injury management, especially for young players with high upside. Teams are increasingly prioritizing long‑term health over short‑term gains, a philosophy that has been reinforced by recent high‑profile injuries that sidelined key contributors for entire seasons. By opting to sit Nacua, the Rams signal a commitment to preserving his durability for the remainder of the campaign, rather than risking a setback that could jeopardize his development and the team’s postseason aspirations.

Looking ahead, the Rams will have a week to reassess Nacua’s condition and potentially reintegrate him for the next game against the Denver Broncos. If the calf continues to improve, he could return to the lineup as early as the following Sunday, providing a much‑needed boost to a passing attack that has struggled to maintain rhythm without him. In the meantime, the onus falls on the remaining receivers and the coaching staff to adapt their scheme and keep the offense productive. The outcome of the Raiders showdown will not only influence the Rams’ win‑loss record but also set the tone for how the team navigates injury challenges as the season enters its critical second half.
